glyph_origin: Bronze inscriptions: Phono-semantic compound (形聲): semantic 貝 (“cowrie; shell”) + phonetic 𠂈. 𠂈 is the original pictograph of 顛 (“to fall headlong”). From the late Western Zhou period, forms with 鼎 instead of 貝 are also attested. Oracle-bone forms are composed of 匕 (“spoon”) and 鼎. These have been read by some scholars as 真, but some of them are better interpreted as 肆 or 煮. In Chu bamboo-slip script, forms with 鼎 became dominant. The legs of 鼎 gradually became graphically confused with 火, and the lower horizontal stroke, left-falling stroke, and dot in Qin-slip and later forms of 真 may be reduced from 火. In the Zeng Hou Yi bamboo slips, an elaborated form with an added 丌 at the bottom is also attested.
